newsitem.title: CHILE: Drought-hit Chile cuts power voltage.
newsitem.headline: Drought-hit Chile cuts power voltage.

text.p: Chilean officials cut power voltage on Wednesday to combat a severe energy crisis caused by drought and said that rationing may be imposed.
Government officials called on consumers to conserve electricity now or face strict rationing later.
The measures will stay in effect for at least a month and could be followed by rationing in two or three weeks, Energy minister Alejandro Jadresic told local media.
"Rationing could be about a month away" if conservation efforts fail to save enough power, said Jaime Bauza, general manager of the country's largest electricity company Endesa.

Chile, with almost no oil reserves, depends on hydroelectric power for about 70 percent of it energy needs. Drought in central and southern regions has cut water levels at dams to a trickle and caused irrigation and water supply problems in some areas.
The emergency measures included a five percent cut in voltage, an energy conservation campaign on radio and television and elimination of decorative lighting on state buildings and in public places.
Spotlights illuminating the Moneda presidential palace in Santiago were turned off last month on the orders of President Eduardo Frei.
Authorities were also in talks with television companies to restrict broadcasting hours to save energy, officials said.
Farm leaders have said the drought will cost the industry hundreds of millions of dollars with sharp falls in some grain crops and a poor quality harvest of fruit, one of Chile's top exports.
A government decree declaring a disaster in some of the worst-hit regions was due to come into effect this week, releasing state funds to help peasant farmers get water.
